title: Why Do We Yawn?
subject: Biology
objective: It isn't low oxygen. The leading idea is brain cooling, and yawns are contagious, especially between people who are close.

fill.q: Giving people extra ____ does not reduce yawning.
A leading idea is that yawning helps ____ the brain.
Yawning often comes before sleep and after ____.
Yawns are ____: seeing someone yawn makes us yawn.

tf.q: We yawn mainly because of low oxygen.
tf.explain: Extra oxygen does not change yawning.
Yawns are seen in the womb.

tf.q: Contagious yawning is stronger among close friends and family.
tf.explain: It is linked to social closeness.

tf.q: Yawning happens only when we are tired.
tf.explain: Also in boredom and state changes.

ar.a: Yawning is not caused by low oxygen.
ar.r: Breathing extra oxygen does not change how often people yawn.
ar.explain: The experiment is the evidence for A.

ar.a: Yawning happens only when we are sleepy.
ar.explain: A is false (boredom, after waking, contagion); R is true.

mcq.q: Which evidence argues against the low-oxygen idea?
options: extra oxygen does not reduce yawning

mcq.q: The brain-cooling idea says a yawn:
options: brings cool air and blood flow to cool the brain

short.q: Why do scientists reject the idea that we yawn for oxygen?
short.solution: In experiments, breathing extra oxygen or carbon dioxide did not change how often people yawned.

short.q: Explain the brain-cooling idea of yawning.
short.solution: The jaw stretch increases blood flow and the deep breath brings in cooler air; together they cool the brain, which may help alertness.
